title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using the declared/requested model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The validator flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, compact provenance-aware run accounting, an explanation of provider-call audit fields, and an artifact-grounded interpretation that the near-zero marginal benefit arose from a validator ceiling effect in a curated parser-validated task bank.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and NetOps workflows. Operators commonly mitigate model errors by pairing generation with downstream tooling: deterministic validators, simulation/emulation, and targeted repair. Prior surveys and tool reports recommend these generate→validate→repair patterns [1]–[3], but provide limited large-scale paired estimates of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution when the same generated candidate is analyzed by both conditions. We preregistered a paired confirmatory experiment to answer the research question: under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720; (3) a concise explanation of provider-call audit fields and run accounting; (4) an evidence-grounded interpretation and prescriptive boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to matter.
sections.related_work: Work on LLMs for NetOps and on verifier-guided generation emphasizes that operational correctness requires multiple V&V primitives: parsing, sequence/order and workflow constraints, invariants (e.g., keep‑one‑uplink‑up), and dynamic runtime properties. Recent surveys and architectural reports synthesize these themes and argue for workflow-centred mitigations that combine static analysis and execution harnesses [1], [2]. Prototype systems and case studies report heterogeneous gains from emulation: in some task regimes static validators already capture most faults; in others emulation uncovers runtime-only failures that static rules miss [3]. Those findings motivated our paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics so that any between-condition discordance can be attributed only to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair invocations.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) with primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and planned Npairs = 720. The preregistration fixed inclusion/exclusion rules, missingness handling (deterministic reseed up to two times for parser failures), a multiplicity plan for exploratory comparisons, and contamination controls (deterministic hashing and binary-version checks). Task generation and inclusion. Confirmatory items come from intent_configuration_repair_v1 deterministic generator, covering three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance after allowed reseeds; the confirmatory run produced zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720. Model and shared_initial_candidate semantics. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses); model_configuration archived requested max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature = null (no explicit client temperature). Per preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics, each pair used exactly one sampled initial candidate (one provider call) and that identical candidate was evaluated by both downstream conditions, isolating downstream guarded-stage effects. Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is a deterministic rule-based checker: vendor-CLI parsing, command canonicalization, sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints (make-before-break, must-be-down-for-fields), protected-interface invariants, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance. The guarded pipeline runs the same validator and then executes the candidate in a sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices. The harness records runtime observations (interface transitions, transient downtime, MTU/VLAN application effects, connectivity consequences) and maps them to runtime-observation rules that can trigger detections absent from the static rule set. Repair policy and provider-call accounting. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model invocation per task, executed only after observing validator and (when applicable) emulation outputs for the guarded condition. Provider-call auditing from deterministic_reconciliation reports model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. Explanation of provider-call audit fields. To avoid ambiguity: model_calls_used is the total hosted-model API calls observed during the run (721). stage_counts reports logical stage attributions: shared_initial_generation = 720 indicates one initial sampled candidate call per paired task (the single shared candidate used by both baseline and guarded evaluations for each pair), and repair = 1 indicates a single repair-stage call occurred across the entire confirmatory set. condition_counts in the audit (for example, entries labelled "shared" or "guarded") reflect how provider calls were attributed to internal orchestration stages or caching keys; they do not imply duplicate independent initial generations per condition in this run. All provider-call audit fields and per-episode call traces are archived in the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation artifacts for independent inspection. Analysis procedures. The primary analysis used a paired-binary executor aligned with McNemar-style exact inference and a paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) as preregistered. The primary analysis used complete-pair handling (no irrecoverable pairs were present).
sections.results: Primary confirmatory counts and inference (artifact-grounded). The paired contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) are n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting and discordant-pair attribution. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation confirm model_calls_used = 721 (stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720; repair = 1). Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the single n10 discordant pair must originate from either (a) a guarded-stage emulation observation that the static validator did not encode, or (b) the single recorded repair-stage invocation. The canonical execution bundle identifies the unique raw_results.jsonl entry where baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1 and links validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields; archived artifacts permit an auditor to inspect that pair_id and repair transcripts. Sensitivity and secondary analyses. The confirmatory execution encountered no irrecoverable technical pairs, so the preregistered sensitivity analysis treating failures as nondetections was not invoked. No exploratory per-class/vendor results exceed the primary-level reporting threshold in this curated set (secondary_results empty in analysis/results.json). Practical numeric summary: Npairs = 720; baseline_success_count = 719; guarded_success_count = 720; paired difference = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% CI = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667].
sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded interpretation. The near-zero aggregate benefit of sandboxed emulation in this run is supported by three artifact-observed factors. (1) Validator ceiling effect and task-rule alignment: the validator explicitly encoded the workflow constraints exercised by the deterministic task generator; representative per-episode validator_trace objects show violation_count = 0 for the vast majority of pairs, producing baseline success rate 719/720 = 0.9986111111 and leaving little headroom for emulation to add detections. (2) Curated parser-validated sample: confirmatory items required parser acceptance and were deterministically generated from intent_configuration_repair_v1, reducing adversarial or out-of-distribution inputs; deterministic_reconciliation shows zero irrecoverable parser exclusions. (3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity: a single repair call (repair = 1) accounts for the lone n10 discordance; provider_call_audit links that repair-stage invocation to the discordant pair. Operational implications. For environments with high-coverage static validators and strong prevalidation of inputs, adding automated sandboxed emulation may offer negligible incremental detection benefit for routine, low-adversary changes. Conversely, in regimes with noisy natural-language intents, adversarial misconfigurations, broader vendor diversity, or where emulation fidelity models long-lived control-plane subtleties, guarded emulation is more likely to surface runtime-only failures. Recommendations grounded in artifacts. Operators should (a) invest in validator rule-coverage for common workflow patterns when low-latency bulk changes are required; (b) reserve guarded sandboxing for high-risk or high-impact changes; (c) use adversarial/fuzzing task banks to identify validator gaps—our archived traces provide concrete seed cases. Limitations and scope. This finding is narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the declared/requested model. The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrow near-zero result for this experimental regime rather than a general negative claim about guarded stages across all NetOps workflows.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call audit shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call); deterministic reconciliation links the single discordant pair to that repair-stage event or to a guarded emulation observation. We conclude that, in this constrained and parser-validated regime, a strong deterministic validator absorbed nearly all detectable faults; whether guarded stages add substantial operational value requires targeted adversarial, cross‑vendor, or higher-fidelity emulation studies. The archived execution manifest and analysis artifacts provide the canonical reproducibility bundle for independent verification.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and provider_call_audit artifacts.
